clue.text: High-flier ruined by exposure in Sun

definitions.text: High-flier ruined by exposure in Sun

parts.words: High-flier ruined by exposure in Sun
parts.note: reads like a celebrity brought down by tabloid revelations in a newspaper called the Sun, but describes the mythical boy whose wax wings melted when he flew too near the sun

explanation.surface: A celebrity's career is wrecked by a kiss-and-tell story in the Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, so 'exposure in Sun' suggests a scandal story; literally it is exposure to the sun's heat that melted the flier's wings in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the son of Daedalus flew on wings of feathers and wax, soared too high, and fell when the sun melted them.

clue.text: Censor accepts new section in poem

indicators.note: accepts means the censor takes in the letter for new

parts.note: Cato the Elder, the Roman statesman known as Cato the Censor

explanation.surface: A censor lets through a fresh passage of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Porcius Cato held the Roman office of censor and is known by that title.
explanation.definitionFit: A long poem such as Dante's is divided into cantos, its main sections.

clue.text: They make up shower curtains artist at home put up

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
in a down entry, putting something up places it above, so these pieces come before the curtains
theatre curtains lowered on stage are drops

explanation.surface: An artist hangs new shower curtains at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' places RA and IN above DROPS in this down entry. 'shower' is rain, not a bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling water droplets are what a burst of rain consists of.

clue.text: "A man' finally solved her cryptic puzzle

definitions.text: "A man' finally solved her cryptic puzzle

parts.words: "A man' finally solved her cryptic puzzle
parts.note: the Theban monster's riddle about what walks on four legs, then two, then three had the reply 'man', which Oedipus finally gave

explanation.surface: A solver at last cracks a female setter's cryptic crossword with the answer 'A man'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic puzzle' suggests a crossword, but it is the riddle the monster of Thebes posed; Oedipus answered 'man' and she died.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged monster outside Thebes set travellers a riddle and was defeated when Oedipus answered it.

clue.text: Nonconformist churchman's back I protected from rain

indicators.note: something shielded from the weather is wrapped up inside a coat, so these letters go inside

parts.note: rain points to the raincoat worn against it, a mack (a variant spelling of mac)

indicators.note: back tells us to read the churchman's title from end to start

parts.note: a churchman is a reverend, abbreviated Rev

explanation.surface: A dissenting vicar's back is kept dry under a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the churchman's title, and 'protected from rain' means wrapped in a raincoat; mack is an older spelling of mac, short for mackintosh.
explanation.definitionFit: An unorthodox independent thinker who refuses to follow the herd is called a maverick, after an unbranded Texas calf.

clue.text: Maiden is under arrest? Just the opposite — that's an error

indicators.note: the surface says maiden-is sits under arrest; the opposite puts those pieces on top in this down entry

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written
an arrest is an apprehension by police

explanation.surface: Is the young woman being arrested? No, the reverse: a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' would put M IS below APPREHENSION; 'Just the opposite' puts it above, in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A misunderstanding or mistaken belief is a wrong grasp of something.

clue.text: One making late appearance (it's in a TV broadcast)

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arriving late turns up on a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges ITS IN A TV. 'late' means dead: the visitor is a ghost, not a latecomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitant is a supernatural visitor, such as the spirit of a dead person who appears.

clue.text: Raise millions to modernise the forces

parts.note: to rear is to raise, as with children or animals
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Spend millions on updating the military.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearming an army can mean re-equipping it with newer weapons, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm a military is to provide it with fresh or improved weapons.

clue.text: Singer, no pro, gets lot wrong

parts.note: being against is the opposite of pro, and contra means against

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the word lot are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An amateur vocalist makes many mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no pro' looks like 'amateur' but means CONTRA, against; 'wrong' rearranges LOT to LTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, or a woman who sings in that range.

clue.text: Opposition is hesitant to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A protest group is reluctant to change its ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges the ten letters of IS HESITANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct contrast or the exact opposite of something is its antithesis.

clue.text: Arranger selecting odd pieces for composer

indicators.note: odd pieces are the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word, taken in turn

explanation.surface: A music arranger picks out unusual bits for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the odd-numbered letters of ARRANGER gives the name of Thomas Arne, the English composer of 'Rule, Britannia!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was an eighteenth-century English composer, best known for 'Rule, Britannia!'.

clue.text: Frosty spell in unfriendly game

parts.note: an unfriendly manner is a cold one
snap is a children's card game where matching cards are called

explanation.surface: An icy atmosphere hangs over a hostile match.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAP is a simple card game in which players shout when two matching cards appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief period of sudden freezing weather is a cold snap.

clue.text: Characteristic tone in old instrument cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the instrument's name is lopped off

parts.note: a timbrel is an ancient tambourine mentioned in the Bible

explanation.surface: A distinctive sound comes from an antique instrument that has been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMBREL, a biblical tambourine, loses its final L to 'cut short'.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive quality of a voice or instrument, apart from pitch and loudness, is its timbre.

clue.text: Charge for conversion as gas is offered, initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A fee for changing over to a new fuel when gas is supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversion' suggests a gas-appliance changeover; here it means exchanging currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Agio is the premium or fee charged when exchanging one currency for another.

clue.text: One sort of bird — and another right outside

indicators.note: outside means these letters go round the little word and

parts.note: another sort of bird, here a goose

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots one species, then a second one just beyond.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'and another' look like a second bird added on, but the little word 'and' is itself fodder, sitting inside the other bird plus right.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a large diving duck of the sawbill family.

clue.text: Call artist a venomous creature

parts.note: to call someone is to ring them on the phone
Frans Hals was a Dutch Golden Age painter

explanation.surface: Someone telephones an artist and calls him a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: HALS is Frans Hals, painter of 'The Laughing Cavalier'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringhals is a southern African spitting cobra, a poisonous snake.

clue.text: Leaves without the slightest difficulty

definitions.meaning: to leave someone property is to bequeath it, pass it on to a later generation
an idiom for winning easily, from a jockey relaxing his grip on the reins

explanation.surface: Departs with no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is a verb meaning bequeaths, not departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing property on to heirs is handing it on; an effortless victory is won easily, as a jockey eases the reins.

clue.text: Small meal? It's hard to say

definitions.meaning: a single bite of food is a modest amount to eat
a long or awkward word or phrase that is difficult to pronounce

explanation.surface: Is it a light snack? Who knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hard to say' reads as 'nobody knows' but describes a tongue-twister of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount taken in one bite of food, and a word difficult to pronounce, both go by this name.

clue.text: Strange sort of small house? Indeed, it was

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the following words are put into an odd new order

parts.note: HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A peculiar little dwelling? Yes, it really was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges SORT OF together with HO, the short form of house. 'it was' marks the definition as an old word: the archaic way of saying 'indeed'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation meaning truly or in truth, now used only jokingly.

clue.text: Absence of authorization for retreat

parts.note: absence of something means there is no such thing
giving the OK is giving approval

explanation.surface: Without permission, someone withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' is a noun here, a quiet hidden corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A small secluded corner or recess where one can withdraw is a nook.

clue.text: Fine Italian instruments you love in Rome

definitions.meaning: violins made by the Amati family of Cremona
the Latin verb for love, second person plural present tense

explanation.surface: Romans adore exquisite Italian violins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' asks for the Latin: 'amatis' means 'you (plural) love'. The Amati family made violins in Cremona.
explanation.definitionFit: Violins made by the Amati family of Cremona, and Latin's second person plural of the verb for love.

clue.text: Was mistress under stress? Sounds like it

indicators.note: sounds like signals that a word said out loud matches the entry

parts.note: something under stress is pulled tight, or taut

explanation.surface: A domineering lover was feeling the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistress' is a schoolmistress, so 'Was mistress' means gave lessons; TAUT is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress instructs pupils, so to have been one is to have given lessons in the past.

clue.text: Involved in begging, a minor?

indicators.note: involved in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Is a child taking part in begging?
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across beggiNG A MINor; the whole clue also describes a street urchin.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a ragged child who might well be found begging.

clue.text: Specify drink — same again?

parts.note: to specify something is to name it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Tell the barman what to pour: the same again?
explanation.walkthrough: 'same again?' looks like a bar order but defines someone who bears the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sharing someone else's name is a namesake, a repeat of the same label.

clue.text: One in exaltation turned up round a village

indicators.note: round means these letters encircle the letter that follows
in a down entry turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an exaltation is the collective noun for larks, so one of them is a lark

explanation.surface: A rapturous visitor arrives at a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exaltation' looks like joy but is the collective noun for larks; LARK turned up gives KRAL, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: In southern Africa a kraal is a traditional village of huts, often enclosed by a fence.

clue.text: Architect leaves sewer after fall

definitions.meaning: Robert ... was an eighteenth-century Scottish architect
in Genesis, after the Fall the first man stitched fig leaves together to cover himself

explanation.surface: A designer quits the drains after taking a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' is someone who sews, not a drain, and 'fall' is the Fall of Man in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Adam designed neoclassical buildings, and the biblical first man sewed fig leaves into aprons after the Fall.

clue.text: Like a resistance force made up without ringleader

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the made-up word wraps round the letter

parts.note: something made up is invented, or fictional
the leader, or first letter, of the word ring is R

explanation.surface: A rebel army was invented and has no head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: FICTIONAL goes round R, the first letter of 'ring'. 'resistance force' is the physics sense, not partisans.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is the force that resists motion between surfaces, so something relating to it is frictional.

clue.text: American statesman noted for his Canterbury relation

definitions.meaning: Benjamin ..., a Founding Father of the United States
in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales one pilgrim is a landowner who tells a story; relation means a tale told

explanation.surface: A US politician famous for his relative from Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' means a narrative, not a family member: Chaucer's pilgrim of this name tells one of the Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin helped found the USA, and a pilgrim landowner tells a tale in Chaucer's Canterbury collection.

clue.text: For example, miss a run

definitions.meaning: a miss is an unmarried woman, an example of someone not wed
in cricket one run scored off a ball is called by this word

explanation.surface: Missing a run, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run scored from one ball is called this; a miss is an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman is unwed, and in cricket one run scored off a delivery shares the word.
